newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-TWO-GOAL HAESSLER EMERGING FROM SLUMP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TWO-GOAL HAESSLER EMERGING FROM SLUMP.

text.p: Three months after he nearly quit the national team in frustration over slumping performances and harsh media criticism, Thomas Haessler was toasted as a hero on Thursday for leading Germany to a convincing win over Armenia.

In Germany's first World Cup qualifying match, Haessler scored two of the first three goals in the side's 5-1 win in Yerevan on Wednesday, drilling in two free kicks and setting up the team's fourth goal.

"Super Haessler" wrote the Bild daily in a fat page one headline on Thursday. The paper had been among his critics for sub-par performances in June when Germany were moving through the European championship en route to the title.
"I've only started feeling better and faster in the last two and a half weeks," Haessler said on Thursday. "Before that I was having a slight slump. But it's fun for me to play again now."
Haessler, 30, the smallest player in the Bundesliga at 1.66 metres, got a warm ovation from the 50,000 fans after he was replaced in the 77th minute.
The Armenian Soccer Association even presented him with two bottles of cognac and an Armenian carpet.
German coach Berti Vogts, who had appealed to Haessler to drop plans to quit the national team after Euro 96, said: "He was excellent. In Armenia, he showed how important he is for us."
